Good morning, everyone. My name is Karen Lopez, and I lead the digital team at a fashion retailer with two hundred stores. Today I want to make one simple point. Customers do not leave a store because of high prices. They leave because of long lines. Last year we asked five thousand customers why they left a store without buying anything. Forty percent said the line was too long. That is our evidence. So we changed three things. First, our staff now use mobile devices to take payments anywhere in the store. Second, customers can pay in the app and walk out. Third, we use data to open more registers before the busy hours. The result? The average waiting time dropped from six minutes to two, and sales increased by twelve percent. So, my main point is this: speed is not a technology project. It is a customer project. If you remember one thing from this talk, please remember that. Thank you.

Thanks, Linda. I agree with Karen about speed, but I want to add a warning. In our grocery stores, we started self-checkout two years ago, and the first months were difficult. Many older customers did not like it. They wanted to talk to a person, not to a machine. So my argument is a little different. Technology is great, but you need people next to it. Today every self-checkout area has one employee who helps the customers. Since then, complaints have dropped by half. And one more thing. Test a new system in a few stores first, not in all your stores at the same time. We learned that the hard way. So my takeaway for the audience is simple: start small, listen to your customers, and keep people in the store. Thank you.

First, the panel was about the future of checkout, and the moderator was Linda Park. Then, Karen Lopez argued that customers leave stores because of long lines. Her evidence was a survey: forty percent of the customers said the line was too long. After that, Tom Bennett said that stores still need people next to the technology. Finally, my main takeaway is that we should test the new system in a few stores first.
